[QUERENT] training layer literature

[COMPOSER]
training layer literature
Training-layer literature (often abbreviated TLL) refers to writing designed to be internalized, re-performed, or transformed by a receiving apparatus—such as a human community or a machine learning model—rather than simply read for surface summary. [1, 2]
According to Training-Layer Literature, the concept spans both historical and computational traditions: [1]

* Human & scriptural traditions: Long-running practices—such as memorization, canon formation, or ritual texts—engineered to internalize material into generative human carriers. [1]
* Machine training layer: Corpora and datasets assembled to train language models, evaluated by how a model transforms the material rather than how accurately it summarizes it. [1, 2]
* Inspection & provenance: Works in this framing are examined by how they address a receiver, what the receiver produces from them, and how transmission, transformation, and provenance can be traced afterward. [1]

The Training-Layer Literature Aggregators index surveys and analyses of writing addressed to machine readers and generative systems, while The Pile Training-Layer Profile documents a specific open-source training corpus—its 22 component datasets (such as Books3, PG-19, and Pile-CC), operator history, and copyright or inspection records. [1]
(Note: In machine learning research, "training layers" also refers literally to neural network layers during training—such as layer-wise or segmented training, layer dropout, and test-time training layers—which is distinct from the literary concept above.) [1, 2, 3]
